resources.string: Shows the time left on a Home Assistant sensor as a running countdown
How long \"Done\" stays up after the timer ends, after which the card disappears on its own. 0 hides it immediately.
Enter which Home Assistant sensor provides the target time. You\'ll find all three values in Home Assistant.
The address you use to open Home Assistant in your browser — without a path and without a trailing /.
In Home Assistant: tap your username at the bottom left → \"Security\" tab → at the very bottom \"Long-lived access tokens\" → \"Create token\". The token is shown only once — copy it right away.

In Home Assistant under \"Developer tools → States\", find your sensor — the entity ID is in the first column. Two kinds of sensor work: those holding a point in time (such as a washing machine\'s finish time) and those holding the time left as a number. A number without a unit is read as minutes.
Tip: Only local addresses like http://homeassistant.local:8123 or http://192.168.x.x:8123 use unencrypted HTTP. For external access (e.g. Nabu Casa) always use https.
✗ %1$s returns \"%2$s\" — no time can be read from that. The sensor needs a point in time or the time left as a number.
✗ Server error (HTTP %1$d). Check the token or entity ID.
✗ No connection: %1$s. Check the URL and network.
